Use a fresh Python kernel to read the complete returned directory and inspect observed mode frequency, native adaptive passes, and Surface EPR. Resolution is offline; this page does not start an AEDT solve.

## 1. Point to the actual returned directory

Retrieve the complete output from Prepare Handoff, or use the `run_dir` produced by Run Directly. In a fresh Python kernel, open the [Analyze notebook](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/f70c3b97f262d54701d710760086433d7ff6c7c1/notebooks/SCGSimExamples/ComponentSimulation/SimplePad/aedt_hfss_eigenmode_analyze.ipynb) and enter that returned directory. Reading results is offline.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.aedt import resolve_results

RETURNED_RUN_DIR = Path("/absolute/path/to/returned/run_dir").expanduser().resolve()
resolved = resolve_results(RETURNED_RUN_DIR)
resolved.show_all_results(show_details=True)
epr = resolved.epr_result()
physics = resolved.physics_results()
benchmark = resolved.simulation_benchmark()
```

Check: the report shows the run receipt, native mode rows, EPR rows when requested, and execution summary. `physics` contains the primary mode results; `benchmark` summarizes execution cost.

## 2. Choose a recorded EPR mode and adaptive pass

This HFSS workflow requests Surface EPR. First check that `epr` is present, then inspect the actual `mode`, `native_pass`, and `status` values in its rows. Use the mode and positive native pass from one row; do not substitute the configured pass limit for an observed pass.

```python
if epr is None:
    raise ValueError("No EPR result was requested; check the run request.")

selections = [
    {
        "mode": row.get("mode"),
        "native_pass": row.get("native_pass"),
        "status": row.get("status"),
    }
    for row in epr.rows
]
print(selections)
```

Choose one row from that output, then enter that row’s exact mode and native pass below.

```python
MODE = 1          # Replace with the selected row's mode.
NATIVE_PASS = 1   # Replace with that same row's native_pass.
```

Check: the selected pair matches one returned row and its recorded status.

::: {.callout-note title="Selecting a row for plotting" collapse="true"}
`show_epr` treats `None` as a wildcard and requires exactly one matching row, so pass both selected values explicitly. Some other result types, such as saved-field rows, omit `native_pass`; this returned adaptive run reports it on EPR rows.
:::

## 3. Read frequency and participation

```python
from scgsim.aedt import plot_epr_result, show_epr

print(physics)
show_epr(epr, mode=MODE, native_pass=NATIVE_PASS)
plot_epr_result(epr, mode=MODE, native_pass=NATIVE_PASS, show_convergence=True)
```

| Report item | Unit and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Primary mode result `frequency_ghz` | GHz; this is the reported mode frequency. |
| EPR row `frequency_hz` | Hz; this value is recorded with the selected EPR row. |
| Surface contribution | `participation` is dimensionless and `energy_j` is J; read the source interface and field-side labels with them. |
| Bulk domain | `energy_j` is J; the displayed participation is calculated as domain energy divided by normalization energy. |
| Junction | `inductive_participation` (`pL`) and `capacitive_participation` (`pC`) are dimensionless. |
| Adaptive history | Frequency and EPR rows are separate records. The EPR selection uses its recorded mode and native pass. |

Check: read each unit from its named result field and keep the row's source labels and status. Interpret only contributions present in the returned request; a missing contribution is not a zero result.

::: {.callout-note title="Other EPR analyses" collapse="true"}
Surface participation and frequency convergence are separate histories. The [saved-field guide](../../course/aedt-saved-fields.qmd) covers AEDT evaluation of saved fields; the [offline EPR guide](../../course/offline-epr.qmd) updates loss assumptions using existing field integrals. They serve different purposes.
:::
